charts.title: How faults were planted and which tests were asked to catch them.
charts.takeaway: Of 47 single faults that passed one calibration point, the backward and contrary checks caught 39 and a wide forward test caught 29; 7 passed every test.
charts.n: 200 single faults planted, 52 crashed a test, 148 scored, 9 equivalent, 47 passed the calibration point

steps.label: Planted: 200 single faults
steps.detail: One arithmetic slip at a time at every arithmetic site of eight small instrument models. Everything here is simulated.

steps.label: 47 quiet faults
steps.detail: Faults that change the output and still pass one calibration point with a known answer.

steps.label: Three-way: backward and contrary checks
steps.detail: Run the model backward against itself and against its contrary. Neither needs a known answer.

steps.label: Comparison: a wide forward test
steps.detail: Many forward reference points with known answers, written before any fault was scored.

steps.label: Forecast: the wide test wins. It caught 29, the checks 39
steps.detail: 11 faults fell only to the backward and contrary checks and 1 only to the wide test. A model that is wrong in a self-consistent way passes both.

charts.title: Quiet faults caught by each test, instrument by instrument.
charts.takeaway: One instrument, the Radon projector, supplies 23 of the 47 faults, and in three instruments the backward and contrary checks caught none.
charts.units: single faults caught, out of those that passed the calibration point in that instrument (the stored share times the stored count)
charts.n: 47 single faults that passed the calibration point, in eight instrument models
charts.no_interval: The result file holds counts per instrument with no interval; the study's sign-flip p for the totals is 0.003.
charts.baseline: The wide forward test on the same faults
charts.threshold: No bar per instrument; the preregistered verdicts are on the totals
